"5b50074f-0fce-5390-894a-fe7e790e061f" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{2}{16 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "5b50074f-0fce-5390-894a-fe7e790e061f" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=4 x$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(4)\,\mathrm{d}x$.

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{1}{4}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $2\cdot \frac{1}{4}=\frac{1}{2}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{2}{16 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{2}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{1}{2}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{1}{2}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{\arctan{\left(4 x \right)}}{2}+C.
$$"] [:db/add "5b50074f-0fce-5390-894a-fe7e790e061f" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "5b50074f-0fce-5390-894a-fe7e790e061f" :question/answer-fields $$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "366d21d4-62b8-54fa-949c-51aee722e657" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=3 x$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(3)\,\mathrm{d}x$.

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{1}{3}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $4\cdot \frac{1}{3}=\frac{4}{3}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{4}{9 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{4}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{4}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{4}{3}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{4 \arctan{\left(3 x \right)}}{3}+C.
$$"] [:db/add "366d21d4-62b8-54fa-949c-51aee722e657" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "366d21d4-62b8-54fa-949c-51aee722e657" :question/answer-fields $$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{1}{3}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $1\cdot \frac{1}{3}=\frac{1}{3}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{1}{9 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{1}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{1}{3}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{\arctan{\left(3 x \right)}}{3}+C.
$$"] [:db/add "8493b404-b397-597e-ad8a-3c8d1066a96e" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "8493b404-b397-597e-ad8a-3c8d1066a96e" :question/answer-fields "15664049-5a30-5d18-a34b-b09f9e4c887f" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{8}{8 x^{2} + 2}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "15664049-5a30-5d18-a34b-b09f9e4c887f" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=2 x$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(2)\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Normalize the denominator:

$$
8 x^{2} + 2=2\left(1+(2 x)^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $4\cdot \frac{1}{2}=2$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{8}{8 x^{2} + 2}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=2\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
2\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=2\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
2 \arctan{\left(2 x \right)}+C.
$$"] [:db/add "15664049-5a30-5d18-a34b-b09f9e4c887f" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "15664049-5a30-5d18-a34b-b09f9e4c887f" :question/answer-fields $$
\int \frac{3}{16 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "281de4d8-737d-52fd-88eb-bfdc5ee854b5" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=4 x$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(4)\,\mathrm{d}x$.

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{1}{4}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $3\cdot \frac{1}{4}=\frac{3}{4}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{3}{16 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{3}{4}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{3}{4}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{3}{4}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{3 \arctan{\left(4 x \right)}}{4}+C.
$$"] [:db/add "281de4d8-737d-52fd-88eb-bfdc5ee854b5" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "281de4d8-737d-52fd-88eb-bfdc5ee854b5" :question/answer-fields "e67daad2-4eb1-599e-ad0c-33dc5036337d" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{4}{x^{2} + 4}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "e67daad2-4eb1-599e-ad0c-33dc5036337d" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{2}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{2})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Normalize the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 4=4\left(1+(\frac{x}{2})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=2\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $1\cdot 2=2$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{4}{x^{2} + 4}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=2\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
2\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=2\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
2 \arctan{\left(\frac{x}{2} \right)}+C.
$$"] [:db/add "e67daad2-4eb1-599e-ad0c-33dc5036337d" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "e67daad2-4eb1-599e-ad0c-33dc5036337d" :question/answer-fields Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "046c3079-1554-5571-917c-f42710075682" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{3}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{3})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Normalize the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 9=9\left(1+(\frac{x}{3})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=3\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{2}{9}\cdot 3=\frac{2}{3}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{2}{x^{2} + 9}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{2}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{2}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{2}{3}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{2 \arctan{\left(\frac{x}{3} \right)}}{3}+C.
$$"] [:db/add "046c3079-1554-5571-917c-f42710075682" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "046c3079-1554-5571-917c-f42710075682" :question/answer-fields \int \frac{4}{x^{2} + 16}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "2a65b5f7-9d91-504f-a06b-aaa4ac2f0122" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{4}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{4})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Normalize the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 16=16\left(1+(\frac{x}{4})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=4\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{1}{4}\cdot 4=1$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{4}{x^{2} + 16}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\arctan{\left(\frac{x}{4} \right)}+C.
$$"] [:db/add "2a65b5f7-9d91-504f-a06b-aaa4ac2f0122" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "2a65b5f7-9d91-504f-a06b-aaa4ac2f0122" :question/answer-fields "b442a1fa-0ba6-5561-87b5-e61b2cab5ed5"] [:db/add "b442a1fa-0ba6-5561-87b5-e61b2cab5ed5" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{4}{x^{2} + 9}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "b442a1fa-0ba6-5561-87b5-e61b2cab5ed5" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{3}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{3})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Normalize the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 9=9\left(1+(\frac{x}{3})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=3\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{4}{9}\cdot 3=\frac{4}{3}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{4}{x^{2} + 9}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{4}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{4}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{4}{3}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{4 \arctan{\left(\frac{x}{3} \right)}}{3}+C.
$$"] [:db/add "b442a1fa-0ba6-5561-87b5-e61b2cab5ed5" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "b442a1fa-0ba6-5561-87b5-e61b2cab5ed5" :question/answer-fields $$
\int \frac{3}{x^{2} + 9}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "08808a54-3c5c-5fcc-8219-93414d371bab" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{3}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{3})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Normalize the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 9=9\left(1+(\frac{x}{3})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=3\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{1}{3}\cdot 3=1$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{3}{x^{2} + 9}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\arctan{\left(\frac{x}{3} \right)}+C.
$$"] [:db/add "08808a54-3c5c-5fcc-8219-93414d371bab" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "08808a54-3c5c-5fcc-8219-93414d371bab" :question/answer-fields Normalize the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 4=4\left(1+(\frac{x}{2})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=2\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{3}{4}\cdot 2=\frac{3}{2}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{3}{x^{2} + 4}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{3}{2}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{3}{2}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{3}{2}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{3 \arctan{\left(\frac{x}{2} \right)}}{2}+C.
$$"] [:db/add "8cd43570-7c53-52ff-ad06-9ec1f1b7c18b" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "8cd43570-7c53-52ff-ad06-9ec1f1b7c18b" :question/answer-fields $$

"baf2420e-d759-52ac-97fe-a2ebcc7925cc" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{3}{25 x^{2} + 4}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "baf2420e-d759-52ac-97fe-a2ebcc7925cc" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{5 x}{2}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{5}{2})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Normalize the denominator:

$$
25 x^{2} + 4=4\left(1+(\frac{5 x}{2})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{2}{5}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{3}{4}\cdot \frac{2}{5}=\frac{3}{10}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{3}{25 x^{2} + 4}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{3}{10}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{3}{10}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{3}{10}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{3 \arctan{\left(\frac{5 x}{2} \right)}}{10}+C.
$$"] [:db/add "baf2420e-d759-52ac-97fe-a2ebcc7925cc" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "baf2420e-d759-52ac-97fe-a2ebcc7925cc" :question/answer-fields "5b50074f-0fce-5390-894a-fe7e790e061f" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{2}{16 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "5b50074f-0fce-5390-894a-fe7e790e061f" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=4 x$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(4)\,\mathrm{d}x$.

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{1}{4}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $2\cdot \frac{1}{4}=\frac{1}{2}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{2}{16 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{2}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{1}{2}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{1}{2}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{\arctan{\left(4 x \right)}}{2}+C.
$$"] [:db/add "5b50074f-0fce-5390-894a-fe7e790e061f" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "5b50074f-0fce-5390-894a-fe7e790e061f" :question/answer-fields $$
\int \frac{4}{9 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "366d21d4-62b8-54fa-949c-51aee722e657" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=3 x$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(3)\,\mathrm{d}x$.

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{1}{3}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $4\cdot \frac{1}{3}=\frac{4}{3}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{4}{9 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{4}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{4}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{4}{3}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{4 \arctan{\left(3 x \right)}}{3}+C.
$$"] [:db/add "366d21d4-62b8-54fa-949c-51aee722e657" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "366d21d4-62b8-54fa-949c-51aee722e657" :question/answer-fields $$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.

$$
\frac{1}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{1}{3}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{\arctan{\left(3 x \right)}}{3}+C.

"15664049-5a30-5d18-a34b-b09f9e4c887f" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{8}{8 x^{2} + 2}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "15664049-5a30-5d18-a34b-b09f9e4c887f" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=2 x$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(2)\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Normalize the denominator:

$$
8 x^{2} + 2=2\left(1+(2 x)^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $4\cdot \frac{1}{2}=2$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{8}{8 x^{2} + 2}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=2\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
2\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=2\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
2 \arctan{\left(2 x \right)}+C.
$$"] [:db/add "15664049-5a30-5d18-a34b-b09f9e4c887f" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "15664049-5a30-5d18-a34b-b09f9e4c887f" :question/answer-fields The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{1}{5}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $2\cdot \frac{1}{5}=\frac{2}{5}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{2}{25 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{2}{5}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{2}{5}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{2}{5}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{2 \arctan{\left(5 x \right)}}{5}+C.
$$"] [:db/add "5302d11c-48b7-5538-b022-7413e48bf00a" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "5302d11c-48b7-5538-b022-7413e48bf00a" :question/answer-fields "e67daad2-4eb1-599e-ad0c-33dc5036337d" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{4}{x^{2} + 4}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "e67daad2-4eb1-599e-ad0c-33dc5036337d" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{2}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{2})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Normalize the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 4=4\left(1+(\frac{x}{2})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=2\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $1\cdot 2=2$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{4}{x^{2} + 4}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=2\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
2\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=2\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
2 \arctan{\left(\frac{x}{2} \right)}+C.
$$"] [:db/add "e67daad2-4eb1-599e-ad0c-33dc5036337d" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "e67daad2-4eb1-599e-ad0c-33dc5036337d" :question/answer-fields $$
x^{2} + 9=9\left(1+(\frac{x}{3})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=3\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{2}{9}\cdot 3=\frac{2}{3}$.

$$

$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{2}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{2}{3}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{2 \arctan{\left(\frac{x}{3} \right)}}{3}+C.
$$"] [:db/add "046c3079-1554-5571-917c-f42710075682" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "046c3079-1554-5571-917c-f42710075682" :question/answer-fields "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{4}{x^{2} + 16}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "2a65b5f7-9d91-504f-a06b-aaa4ac2f0122" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{4}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{4})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Normalize the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 16=16\left(1+(\frac{x}{4})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=4\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{1}{4}\cdot 4=1$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{4}{x^{2} + 16}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\arctan{\left(\frac{x}{4} \right)}+C.
$$"] [:db/add "2a65b5f7-9d91-504f-a06b-aaa4ac2f0122" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "2a65b5f7-9d91-504f-a06b-aaa4ac2f0122" :question/answer-fields "b442a1fa-0ba6-5561-87b5-e61b2cab5ed5"] [:db/add "b442a1fa-0ba6-5561-87b5-e61b2cab5ed5" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{4}{x^{2} + 9}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "b442a1fa-0ba6-5561-87b5-e61b2cab5ed5" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{3}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{3})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Normalize the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 9=9\left(1+(\frac{x}{3})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=3\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{4}{9}\cdot 3=\frac{4}{3}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{4}{x^{2} + 9}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{4}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{4}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{4}{3}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{4 \arctan{\left(\frac{x}{3} \right)}}{3}+C.
$$"] [:db/add "b442a1fa-0ba6-5561-87b5-e61b2cab5ed5" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "b442a1fa-0ba6-5561-87b5-e61b2cab5ed5" :question/answer-fields "baf2420e-d759-52ac-97fe-a2ebcc7925cc" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int \frac{3}{25 x^{2} + 4}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "baf2420e-d759-52ac-97fe-a2ebcc7925cc" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{5 x}{2}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{5}{2})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Normalize the denominator:

$$
25 x^{2} + 4=4\left(1+(\frac{5 x}{2})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{2}{5}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{3}{4}\cdot \frac{2}{5}=\frac{3}{10}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{3}{25 x^{2} + 4}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{3}{10}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{3}{10}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{3}{10}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{3 \arctan{\left(\frac{5 x}{2} \right)}}{10}+C.
$$"] [:db/add "baf2420e-d759-52ac-97fe-a2ebcc7925cc" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "baf2420e-d759-52ac-97fe-a2ebcc7925cc" :question/answer-fields $$
\frac{1}{6}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{1}{6}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

"9b644cf3-d6d1-5446-bbbf-2908d8c05cdd"] [:db/add "9b644cf3-d6d1-5446-bbbf-2908d8c05cdd" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] [:db/add "9b644cf3-d6d1-5446-bbbf-2908d8c05cdd" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{5 x}{3}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{5}{3})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Normalize the denominator:

$$
25 x^{2} + 9=9\left(1+(\frac{5 x}{3})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{3}{5}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{3}{5}=\frac{1}{5}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{3}{25 x^{2} + 9}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{5}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{1}{5}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{1}{5}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{\arctan{\left(\frac{5 x}{3} \right)}}{5}+C.
$$"] [:db/add "9b644cf3-d6d1-5446-bbbf-2908d8c05cdd" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "9b644cf3-d6d1-5446-bbbf-2908d8c05cdd" :question/answer-fields $$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] ["e67daad2-4eb1-599e-ad0c-33dc5036337d" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{x}{2}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{1}{2})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Normalize the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 4=4\left(1+(\frac{x}{2})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=2\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $1\cdot 2=2$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{4}{x^{2} + 4}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=2\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
2\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=2\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
2 \arctan{\left(\frac{x}{2} \right)}+C.
$$"] ["e67daad2-4eb1-599e-ad0c-33dc5036337d" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] ["e67daad2-4eb1-599e-ad0c-33dc5036337d" :question/answer-fields "4fdc3313-e82f-5314-a725-4ffa5fbda3ad"] Normalize the denominator:

$$
x^{2} + 16=16\left(1+(\frac{x}{4})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=4\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $\frac{1}{8}\cdot 4=\frac{1}{2}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{2}{x^{2} + 16}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{2}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{1}{2}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{1}{2}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{\arctan{\left(\frac{x}{4} \right)}}{2}+C.
$$"] ["de3afc7b-6342-5c89-b7b3-754c8842d886" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] ["de3afc7b-6342-5c89-b7b3-754c8842d886" :question/answer-fields "95437f4a-a7d2-5799-ba81-e8a6c4c235ba"] ["45ebda02-1c0c-5192-b4c8-f1d420459040" :question/id #uuid "45ebda02-1c0c-5192-b4c8-f1d420459040"] ["45ebda02-1c0c-5192-b4c8-f1d420459040" :question/problem "Find an antiderivative.

$$

Choose the antiderivative. In each choice, $C$ is an arbitrary constant."] ["45ebda02-1c0c-5192-b4c8-f1d420459040" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=\frac{3 x}{2}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(\frac{3}{2})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Normalize the denominator:

$$
9 x^{2} + 4=4\left(1+(\frac{3 x}{2})^2\right).
$$

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{2}{3}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $1\cdot \frac{2}{3}=\frac{2}{3}$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \frac{4}{9 x^{2} + 4}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{2}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\frac{2}{3}\left(\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=\frac{2}{3}\left(\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
\frac{2 \arctan{\left(\frac{3 x}{2} \right)}}{3}+C.
$$"] ["45ebda02-1c0c-5192-b4c8-f1d420459040" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] ["45ebda02-1c0c-5192-b4c8-f1d420459040" :question/answer-fields "246dd6bc-5896-51cb-8976-0e0583e515c0"]
